module_name: Education Access E-Learning Academy — Form One Mathematics
title: Form One Mathematics Assessment Framework
purpose: To establish a structured, continuous and evidence-based assessment system for measuring mathematical knowledge, understanding, procedural fluency, reasoning, application and learner mastery.
assessment_principles: Assessment must align with the approved curriculum and intended learning outcomes.
Assessment must measure understanding as well as procedural accuracy.
Learners must receive regular and constructive feedback.
Assessment must provide opportunities for independent mathematical thinking.
Assessment evidence must be accurate, authentic and properly recorded.
Assessment results must inform teaching, learning support and progression.
Assessment must promote fairness, accessibility and academic integrity.

assessment_types.name: Diagnostic Assessment
assessment_types.timing: Before beginning a new topic or learning unit.
assessment_types.purpose: Identify learners' existing knowledge, prior understanding and possible learning gaps.

assessment_types.name: Formative Assessment
assessment_types.timing: Throughout the teaching and learning process.
assessment_types.purpose: Monitor understanding and provide feedback while learning is taking place.

assessment_types.name: Knowledge Check
assessment_types.timing: At the end of an appropriate lesson or learning unit.
assessment_types.purpose: Determine whether learners understand the concepts and procedures taught.

assessment_types.name: Application Assessment
assessment_types.timing: After relevant concepts and procedures have been taught.
assessment_types.purpose: Evaluate the ability to apply mathematical knowledge to practical and unfamiliar situations.

assessment_types.name: Friday Weekly Assessment
assessment_types.timing: At the end of each learning week.
assessment_types.purpose: Review and evaluate the mathematical knowledge and skills developed during the week.

assessment_types.name: Summative Assessment
assessment_types.timing: At the end of a defined topic, term or programme assessment period.
assessment_types.purpose: Evaluate the extent to which intended curriculum outcomes have been achieved.

assessment_types.name: Evidence and Mastery Assessment
assessment_types.timing: Throughout the programme and at designated mastery review points.
assessment_types.purpose: Verify mathematical competence through multiple forms of learner evidence.

assessment_components.assessment_focus: Understanding of concepts and mathematical procedures.
assessment_components.evidence: Notes, explanations and responses to instructional questions.

assessment_components.assessment_focus: Accuracy, fluency and correct application of procedures.
Transfer of mathematical knowledge to practical problems.
Reflection and identification of learning needs.

criteria.description: Ability to explain mathematical concepts and relationships.
Ability to select and perform appropriate mathematical procedures.
Ability to explain and justify mathematical solutions.
Ability to solve mathematical problems in practical contexts.
Ability to present mathematical ideas and solutions clearly.

performance_levels.name: Beginning
performance_levels.description: Requires substantial guidance and demonstrates limited understanding.

performance_levels.name: Developing
performance_levels.description: Demonstrates partial understanding and completes familiar tasks with support.

performance_levels.name: Proficient
performance_levels.description: Demonstrates secure understanding and independently completes expected tasks.

performance_levels.name: Advanced
performance_levels.description: Demonstrates strong understanding and applies mathematical reasoning to unfamiliar problems.

scoring_guidance.principle: Assessment scores must reflect the requirements and learning outcomes of the specific assessment.
rules: Allocate marks according to the assessment instrument.
Award marks for valid mathematical methods and reasoning where appropriate.
Record actual scores and maximum available marks.
Do not treat completion of learning activities as automatic evidence of mastery.
scoring_guidance.grading_note: Specific grading boundaries, examination weightings and institutional reporting scales must be configured according to applicable national and institutional assessment requirements.

feedback_requirements: Indicate which learning outcomes require further development.

learner_progress_tracking.progression_rule: Progression decisions must be based on relevant and sufficient assessment evidence, professional teacher judgement and demonstrated learning outcomes.

quality_assurance.validity: Assessment must measure the intended mathematical knowledge and competencies.
quality_assurance.reliability: Marking criteria must support consistent assessment decisions.
quality_assurance.fairness: Assessment conditions must be appropriate and equitable.
quality_assurance.authenticity: Learner evidence must represent genuine individual performance.
quality_assurance.transparency: Assessment instructions and expectations must be communicated clearly.
quality_assurance.curriculum_alignment: Assessment instruments must be checked against the applicable TIE 2023 Form One Mathematics curriculum.
quality_assurance.record_management: Assessment records must be maintained accurately and securely.

implementation_responsibilities.learner: Participate in assessments, complete assigned tasks honestly and use feedback to improve.
implementation_responsibilities.teacher: Design assessments, evaluate performance, provide feedback and validate mastery.
implementation_responsibilities.learning_facilitator: Support learner participation and identify learning difficulties.
implementation_responsibilities.platform: Organise assessment activities, display permitted results and maintain learner evidence records.
implementation_responsibilities.academic_administration: Monitor assessment quality, curriculum alignment and institutional reporting.

completion_message: Assessment is not simply the measurement of marks. It is a continuous process of understanding, feedback, improvement and verified mathematical achievement.
